The Score-Driven Recursion's Derivatives to the Fifth Order, R Route

Source: R/gas_fifth.R
dot-gas_fifth_run.Rd

Propagates the jets of the filtered predictor over three directions through the recursion and returns the contractions of term_fifth(). .gas_fifth_scalar() serves a term without subformulas, whose chart is the same at every observation, and .gas_fifth_sub() a term with subformulas, whose chart is read per observation; both run .gas_fifth_run().

Usage

.gas_fifth_run(term, eta, score, g, seed, blocks_data, dirs, chart_at)

.gas_start_jet(ch, m, dirs)

.gas_fifth_scalar(term, eta, y, score, psi, g, seed, blocks_data, dirs)

.gas_fifth_sub(term, eta, y, score, psi, g, seed, blocks_data, dirs)

.gas_sub_chart_fun(tm, psiv, cols, m, dirs)

Arguments

term

A built term.

eta

The static part of the predictor.

score

The score callback of term_filter(), which gives the value of the driving score.

g

The weights against which the fifth derivative is contracted, one per observation.

seed

The derivative of the static predictor in the caller's unknowns.

blocks_data

The model's derivative arrays, as set out above.

dirs

The three directions.

chart_at

A function of a row returning the jets omega, a and b there.

ch

The chart's jets at the group's first observation.

m

The number of unknowns.

y

The response.

psi

The term's parameters, named as term_params().

tm

A built score-driven term, with or without subformulas.

psiv

Its parameters in the order of term_params(): the parameter scale for a parameter without a subformula, the coefficients for a developed one.

cols

The columns of those parameters among the unknowns.

Value

.gas_start_jet() the jet of the starting level; the others as term_fifth().

Details

At each observation the level is \(f_t = \omega + \sum_i a_i s_{t-i} + \sum_j b_j f_{t-j}\), and its jet is the sum of the products of jets (.gas_jet_times()). The score's jet is composed from the family's derivative arrays by .gas_score_jet(). The orders below the fifth are carried along every subset of the directions, so this route is a second, independent computation of what term_curvature(), term_third() and term_fourth() return. The starting level of a group is read off the fixed point at the group's first observation, as at the lower orders.

.gas_sub_chart_fun() returns the chart at a row for a term whose values are read per observation: each base parameter and each cross loading is \(h(z^\top u)\), with \(z\) its design row among the unknowns (a unit vector for a parameter without a subformula), and the autoregressive coefficients come from .gas_map_jets(). The result at a row carries x, the cross loadings' jets in the order of the term's pairs (partner, lag).
